description: This topic covers India's protected areas, their geographical locations, and wildlife conservation efforts. It is a highly crucial section of Static General Knowledge for competitive exams.

sections.title: Basic Concepts and History
sections.description: Key terminologies related to wildlife conservation and the history of their development in India.

key_concepts.explanation: A protected area established for the conservation of wildlife and biodiversity. Strict rules apply here, and human activities like grazing, hunting, and logging are completely prohibited.
A designated area where animal habitats and their surroundings are protected from any sort of disturbance. Limited human activities are permitted here.
Large protected areas divided into three zones: Core, Buffer, and Transition. They are meant to demonstrate a balanced relationship between humans and the biosphere.

historical_events.significance: It was established as India's first National Park. It is now globally renowned as Jim Corbett National Park, located in Uttarakhand.
Enacted by the Government of India for the protection of plant and animal species, effectively banning hunting and regulating wildlife trade.

sections.title: Major National Parks of North and East India
sections.description: A list of significant national parks in North and East India and their endemic wildlife species.

geographical_data.key_characteristics: It is the largest national park in India by area and is globally famous for its high population of Snow Leopards.
A UNESCO World Heritage Site, famous for hosting two-thirds of the world's Great One-horned Rhinoceroses.
The only floating national park in the world, located on Loktak Lake. It is the last natural habitat of the endangered Sangai (dancing deer).
It is India's first and only 'Mixed' UNESCO World Heritage Site, known for its unique high-altitude ecosystems.

sections.title: Major National Parks of Central, West and South India
sections.description: Prominent protected areas located in other regions of India and their unique geographical features.

geographical_data.key_characteristics: It is the only natural habitat of the Asiatic Lions in the entire world.
Famous for saving the Barasingha (Swamp Deer) from extinction. It is the first tiger reserve to officially introduce a mascot, 'Bhoorsingh'.
Known for its pristine tropical evergreen forests and the endangered Lion-tailed Macaque.
Renowned for its diurnal Royal Bengal Tigers and features a historic 10th-century fort within its boundaries.

sections.title: Tiger Reserves and Project Tiger
sections.description: India's flagship conservation initiative to save the Bengal Tiger from extinction.

historical_events.significance: An ambitious conservation program launched from Jim Corbett National Park to ensure a viable population of the Bengal tiger.

key_associations.extra_info: It is the largest tiger reserve in India in terms of total geographical area.
This specific forest is recognized as the inspiration behind Rudyard Kipling's famous classic, 'The Jungle Book'.
It is the only national park and tiger reserve located in the state of Bihar.
Highly acclaimed for its successful Hornbill nest adoption program and conservation efforts.

sections.title: Exam-Oriented Important Facts
sections.description: Crucial one-liner facts, superlatives, and key data points frequently tested in competitive exams.

important_facts.fact: The smallest National Park in India is South Button Island National Park, located in the Andaman and Nicobar Islands.
Madhya Pradesh is known as the 'Tiger State of India' because it has the highest number of tigers and the maximum number of national parks in the country.
India's first Marine National Park was established in the Gulf of Kutch, Gujarat, to protect the fragile coral reefs and marine life.
As of recent updates, India has over 50 Tiger Reserves, with newer additions including the 54th Veerangana Durgavati (Madhya Pradesh) and 55th Dholpur-Karauli (Rajasthan).
